# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MC

PJam projects — diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is i
n preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change — inclu
ding in\n> breaking ways — while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [
tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg

/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/se

ttings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and th

en land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.m

cpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects — from CI, scripts, or your own agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with i

t today:

* **Discover your resources** — list your projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the

other routes need is
 self-serve
* **Validate a server** — connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot
* **Run the
doctor** — the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAu
th grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources** — the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute p
rimitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and
prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients** — list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude
`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n
MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as
`expectedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename — a rename\n does not rotate the co
nfig, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent\n one — and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* *
*Manage a project's environments** — list, read, create, edit, archive, and\n restore the named execution bundles (host + optiona
l server group + optional\n pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval suites and goals run against,\n and **preview** what on
e resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies** — name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link — and *
*read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-approval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites** — crea
te a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no cr
edits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously** — create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, the
n poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n
tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts** — complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your
CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n
write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn** — send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the
platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n s
erver-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback** — report a bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the M

CPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers y
ou have already added to a project in the\nhosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see\n[Not in the API yet](#not-in

-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is pat

h-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam AP

I key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/a
pi/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type:

application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/a

pi-keys)
 in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name
it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and never\

n stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediat

ely.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-req
uest authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never re

ach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot
manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke

keys in
> the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API k

ey like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to
 source control or ship it
in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a re
placement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API keys

**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: "ORPHANED_KEY"`, the key
is no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key\nfrom [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-k

eys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Reads**
— the catalog listings and eval-run polling — are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query\nparameters

.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource obj
ect directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }` — `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error
| `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |\n\n**Pagination.** Collections a
re cursor-based. Pass the previous response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,\nquery pa
rameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque — don't parse them.\n\n**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a
runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything
— author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetach
es execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,\n`cancelle
